releases.title: Neighbours, stickers and runners
releases.pitch: Walk between ForkMesh Worlds, react to messages with stickers, and keep runners in hand from the desktop and the iPhone.

releases.title: Face swap, a new Market and What's new
releases.pitch: Calls get face swap and background blur, the Market gets a fresh look, and the app tells you what changed.

releases.title: The Living Code City
releases.pitch: ForkMesh becomes a shared three-dimensional developer world backed by independently operated repository mirrors.

releases.title: The Agent Mesh
releases.pitch: The release where ForkMesh starts to feel alive. Open an issue, hand it to an AI agent, and watch a real pull request show up — all without leaving the mesh.

releases.title: Autonomous Agents
releases.pitch: Collaboration stopped being a one-person job.

releases.title: Identity & Rewards
releases.pitch: ForkMesh added optional community-funded incentives for healthy mirror operators.

releases.title: Collaborate Anywhere
releases.pitch: The web caught up to the desktop, and ForkMesh went mobile.

releases.title: Genesis
releases.pitch: The first commit. A bet that source code shouldn't be locked to a single forge.

notes.text: On Linux, a ForkMesh app-menu icon left over from an old install now opens the current app instead of an outdated copy that stopped with a mirror Actions error.
Marketing: every table, on the web and in the desktop app, now sorts by any column when you click its header; click again to reverse the order.
Marketing's ready X post now has an optional field for the post's link when you mark it posted, so the link stays with the post's history.
Marketing: double-click a row in a channel's Recorded numbers to correct its numbers, and the browser extension no longer reads a post's views on an X profile as the account's.
Video messages with a face and background start reliably on slower devices, and a voice that cannot start now says so instead of blaming the face.
On iPhone Duo the row for the item open on the right stays highlighted in the list, as on the desktop.
On a foldable's inner display the app shows lists on the left and the open item on the right, like the desktop and iPhone Duo.
On iPhone Duo's inner display the app shows lists on the left and the open item on the right, like the desktop, with a Liquid Glass side rail when the phone is on its side.
On the website, a repository's Code, Issues and Pull requests tabs no longer vanish when the plugin list cannot be read, and "fixes #N" in a pull request comment links that issue again.
ForkMesh World shows again where it is embedded in forkmesh.com pages opened at www.forkmesh.com.
The iPhone app no longer freezes for a moment at launch while it loads your saved chat history, and both phone apps put it back faster.
The admin button is back in the dashboard header for admins who were signed in from another ForkMesh page.

Glasses Alert on iPhone and Android now also rings for cameras with Bluetooth on nearby, such as GoPro, Insta360, DJI, Canon, Nikon and Sony cameras, body cameras, dash cams, security cameras and camera drones.

Shortcuts: a repository with no shortcuts now offers Add starter shortcuts, five ready-made prompts (review your changes, UX audit, stale-code cleanup, docs refresh, feature retirement) you can commit for everyone.
Claude Code agents the desktop starts no longer spend tokens refreshing a hidden status line every 30 seconds.
The High memory usage window no longer ends ForkMesh by accident: whatever started it, its helpers and the display server can't be killed from there, by hand or automatically.
Shortcuts and workflows you start from your phone run right away again: the tap counts as your approval, so nobody has to click Allow on the desktop.
On iPhone and Android, an agent's question now shows at the bottom of its transcript with tap-to-pick answers, and typing in the follow-up box answers it.

Restart computer from your phone now works when another user is on the screen or nobody is logged in, once you turn on Settings, General, Let my phones restart this computer; until then the phone says which setting to turn on.
Restarting the desktop no longer pings you again for every pull request still waiting for check approval.

When two of the three servers are down, ForkMesh stays up read-only: pages, repositories, clones and downloads keep working, and saving changes shows a clear read-only message until the servers recover.
Android: group calls use your chosen call face, background and voice, and send a live moving face when other people's links are too weak for your video.
Desktop agent transcripts now show Claude Code development intent and command lifecycle updates.
Running sub-sessions now show as a steady, draggable Sub-sessions card in the side panels, and Control Tower gets those panels as a right column beside the conversation.

Running a special agent such as the CEO from the Workflows page now asks you to approve its file right there and then shows the run's steps and log, and a run that cannot start stays in Recent runs with the reason.
Codex transcripts now show remote control status, MCP startup progress and failures, and thread settings changes without flagging internal moderation metadata as missing.
A ping's detail page has a back link at the top that returns you to your list of pings.

The new repository form says plainly that Import from GitHub copies issues and pull requests but not the code, shows whether the result will be public or private before you create it, and links a new step-by-step guide to backing up a GitHub repository.
On Linux, ForkMesh adds itself to the applications menu the first time it runs, so you can find it again after closing it.

Signing in on the desktop checks the email you type, so a suggested username that is not yours no longer reports a correct password as wrong; the password box has an eye button, and a lockout says how long to wait.
Workflows lists your desktop's workflows and special agents and runs them there, and Free disk space has a button that runs it on your desktop.
Free disk space has a button in the Workflows list that runs it on your desktop.
Version 1.5.0 brings the desktop, Android and iPhone apps to the same version number, and every platform starts it at build 0.

Poker arrives in the Market: play no-limit Texas Hold'em with other ForkMesh users for virtual chips, with a dealer, bots to fill seats, side pots, turn clocks and casino sounds, on the web, the desktop, iPhone and Android.

Android: with several desktops on your account, the Desktops page shows each one's status and lets you pick one, Runs on lists every desktop, and the lights by the clock stack the desktops and core nodes.
Android: with Diagnostics on, the status dots, the desktop and core node lights with tiny CPU, memory and disk bars, and filled app charts sit by the clock and the camera cutout.
Android: Settings > Appearance has a Layout choice, Control Tower or Focus, which the CRM follows.

Android: the CRM has Home, Contacts, Pipeline, Activity and More sections, a shorter add form and a contact page with Overview, Activity and Notes tabs, and adding a contact whose email is already in the CRM offers to open them or add the new details.

Android: agent tiles show live token flow, file churn, badges and a done bar, two token charts sit under the status bar, merges can set aside desktop edits, every desktop's agents share one list, and agent alerts open a loading page with Try again.

Android: calls reconnect after a network drop, end with a clear message when they cannot connect, keep going in a small window you can drag when you go back to the chat, show your camera with the other person's name until their video arrives, play video calls on the loudspeaker, and have a Diagnose button that explains call problems.
Android: Stats release tiles show a rebuilt download's build number from build 1.

Android: pull requests look like GitHub's, with an Open, Merged or Closed pill, the description as the first comment, a Merged entry and a done box, and New pull request compares branches and can send to a fork on another instance; Send to agent on a failed run's log sends the failing step and the end of the log.
Android: each Inbox ping shows the logo of the instance it came from under its icon.

Android: in DJ Studio, hold a queued song for its menu, drag it onto a deck as soon as your finger moves across the queue, see who added each jam song and when, and a song added while nothing plays starts right away.
Android: chat media and opened files are saved under names that cannot step outside their folder or clash with another message's file.

Android: a bot line or member shown as Guest switches to the sender's account once the server confirms their device, several new devices in a private chat share one approve-or-block banner, and restoring your identity key after a reinstall keeps your chat key and safety numbers.
Android: links in chats show preview cards like on iPhone; in shared rooms a preview loads only when you tap it, and previews never reach private or local network addresses.

The Android tour offers Essentials, Advanced and The whole shebang with a live copy of each screen you can try, and a new install asks for no permissions at launch, only when a feature first needs one.
Android: group calls run on ForkMesh's own media engine with a code everyone can compare to check the call is end-to-end encrypted, and show a live moving face when a link is too weak for video.

Android: the Speech playground reads any text aloud in the voice, speed and pitch you pick, highlights each word as it speaks and saves the audio, and Logs and Diagnostics open from the You hub and the Market.
Sign-up and password reset emails now reach Yahoo and other strict mail providers, and an address is no longer blocked from future emails when a provider refused one because of our own mail setup.

When a pull request is merged, its conversation shows a Merged entry, and a merged or closed pull request no longer offers merge, approve or request-changes controls on the website, desktop or iPhone.

Pull requests on iPhone look like GitHub's: an Open, Merged or Closed pill, the description as the first comment, and a New pull request form that compares branches and can send the pull request to a copy of the repository on another ForkMesh instance.
Claiming or linking a node with your password now asks for your authenticator code when two-factor sign-in is on.
Webhook posts in a public channel now notify only people who opened that channel, and each account can create up to 5 channels an hour.
A phone paired with a code is a guest until your account confirms it is yours; terminals, secrets, wallet and fleet controls stay with confirmed phones.
Workflows and shortcuts committed in a repository now also need your approval before a phone, a package or a schedule toggle can run them.
Automatic updates now install only releases signed by ForkMesh that are newer than the version you run.

Workflows and special agents committed in a repository now run on a schedule or a repository event only after you approve the file on this desktop, and a change to the file or to a script it runs asks again.
Invoicing on the web: when saving, emailing or recording a payment fails, the reason and what to do next now show inside the open dialog instead of behind it.
Tapping an agent alert now opens its page while it loads, finds agents on your other desktops and runners, and offers Try again instead of a blank page.
On a phone, the web issue and pull request lists are more compact, and the New issue, refresh and view buttons now line up at one height.
Deleting an agent now also ends anything still running in its worktree, so the phone no longer shows a leftover row named after the branch with "(deleted)".
The CRM on iPhone has a new compact layout with Home, Contacts, Pipeline, Activity and More, and a Control Tower or Focus layout plus the theme switch right under its settings.
Adding a CRM contact no longer fails with a false "already uses that email" after a double tap or a dropped connection, and an address already in the CRM now says who has it and lets you open them.

A shared pull request link now previews the pull request itself: its state, reviews and approvals, comment counts, files and lines changed, the six code health scores and the faces of everyone taking part.

In the new interface, dots, arrows, labels and panels no longer sit on a box of a slightly different colour: every element now shares its section's background, and each theme uses one colour per role.
Invoicing on Android: create and edit invoices for CRM contacts, email them and send reminders, record payments, and see when each one is opened, viewed and paid.
Invoicing on iPhone: create and edit invoices for CRM contacts, email them and send reminders, record payments, and see when each one is opened, viewed and paid.
Invoicing has its own desktop page: create, email, track and record payments on invoices without leaving the app, and see a CRM contact's invoices on their card.
New Invoicing plugin: bill CRM contacts, email invoices with a view-and-pay link, and see when each one is opened, viewed and paid.
The Ecosystem directory has a new Work & client management section with 13 agency and client-portal tools, each compared with ForkMesh.

New projects can start Empty, with nothing installed and nothing running until you add it from the Market; removing a feature now also stops its background work, and the built-in browser loads only when you first open a page, so the desktop on Linux starts with about 30 MB less memory.
Workflows on iPhone now also lists your desktop's workflows and special agents and runs them on the desktop, and Free disk space runs on your desktop from the phone.
The new interface has two layout modes in the view menu: Control Tower, compact with every control in view, and Focus, one thing at a time; one choice now sets both the Agents and the Git page.
When the desktop was built without the embedded browser, the Browser tab now has an Install embedded browser button that installs it and rebuilds the app.
Sessions now open with side panels for progress, outputs, sources, background tasks, changes, context and tools, which you can drag into any order; the Agents page has them too in a new Details tab.
With more than one desktop, Agents now lists every desktop's agents together, each labelled with its desktop.
Agent transcripts now show Claude Code version control state changes such as pushes.
Clicking a workflow on the Workflows page opens a details pane on the right with its settings and every action, and shows its latest run's log at the bottom right.

The web CRM now has the desktop's layout, with every list and pipeline in a column on the left and all its pages there, and each member can connect their own Zoho Mail to send and sync from their own mailbox.
Running a workflow now sparkles the new run into Recent runs and shows its steps right away, each one animating as it starts and finishes, with the live log underneath.
The workflow editor is more compact: steps show as numbered cards with their last result, chips show the schedule, last and next run and success rate, and the runs sit beside the form.
Forking forkmesh/forkmesh on the website now copies its code into your fork, so you can clone it, push branches and open a pull request back to ForkMesh.
The token charts under the Dynamic Island now always show and update every second, and agent tile borders move while a reply is still streaming.
Edit on an inline comment in a pull request's Files changed tab now opens the editor right there, and closing or saving any comment edit puts keyboard focus back on its Edit button.
The desktop no longer opens on an empty Select a repository page: it reopens your last repository, or opens Home when there is none.
Claude Code agents are stopped from reading a large file whole and are told to search it and read the part they need, which keeps their context smaller.

Tool efficiency has a Trends view: twelve charts for the last hour, 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days, from agents running, memory and CPU to tool errors, efficiency, run time and cost, each against the period before and marked where the build, memory or agent limit changed.
A .worktreeinclude file in your repository now copies the ignored files it lists, such as .env, into each new agent worktree.
Drop files on the desktop prompt to attach images or mention files, type / to open the command menu, and open a session's folder in VS Code, Cursor, Zed or your file manager from its menu.

The desktop Agents workspace picks up Claude Code desktop's keys: Ctrl+Tab between sessions, Ctrl+Shift+D, Ctrl+` and Ctrl+Shift+B for the diff, terminal and browser, Shift+Tab to change the permission mode, and Ctrl+/ to list them all.
Actions runs no longer fail part-way through a build when another ForkMesh window or test opens on the same computer.

In #welcome on the web, a Welcome button sends an animated genie spider to greet everyone, picked at random from 10 entrances: a silk drop, a magic lamp, confetti, a magic carpet, sparkles, bouncing, balloons, a WELCOME web, fireworks and peekaboo.
The desktop Market opens without waiting for package previews, which appear as each one loads.
Sending a chat message no longer freezes the desktop for a moment while it saves its message counter to disk.

The Network page's node list is much narrower: each cell shows two facts, one per line, the node's role, owner, place and version sit under its name, columns that are empty for the current filter are hidden, and sorting moved to a Sort menu on the All / Core / Runners bar.
An agent started by a workflow now shows a link at the top back to its workflow.
Right-click an agent on the desktop and choose Send to another desktop to have one of your other computers carry on its work; it stops here and continues there on the same branch.
World forms no longer trigger the browser's missing-name warnings, and the World chat's Discord refresh no longer errors when one channel cannot be read.
When the World cannot use your camera it now says why: blocked for the site, in use by another app, or no camera found.
Turning the camera on in the World no longer flashes and switches off when your browser cannot track your face: with Also send video ticked, your camera keeps sending video.
Removing a plugin whose data stays on disk now says so in a notice instead of a dialog that had to be clicked, and Market previews in WebP show on Linux without Qt's extra image plugins.
The Agents list shows each agent's task progress next to its title, like 2/5 and what it is doing now, and agents now build with twice as many parallel jobs on machines with memory to spare.
The desktop window opens about twice as fast: installed package pages now load just after the window appears, and the Claude app's own log lines no longer land in ForkMesh's terminal.
With Match the instance's theme turned on, the View menu now shows which theme the instance is sending, like "Match the instance's theme (BLT)".
In the new design, the View menu has a Git layout choice: Compact brings back the Git page with changed files on top, history underneath and the branch picker in the history header.
Agent sessions now pin a live task list under the transcript, like Claude Code desktop: Claude's todos and tasks, Codex plans and each subagent's own list update in place as the agent works.
Face Changer now runs inside the desktop app and, on Linux, becomes a ForkMesh Camera you can pick in Google Meet or any other call app.
You can now delete your own pull request reviews (an approval or change request keeps its verdict and loses only its text), and edit or delete your inline comments right in the Files changed tab.

Open pull requests no longer show a block of AI instructions: a Diff and files box links the diff, the patch and every changed file, and Summarize in ChatGPT opens ChatGPT asking for a summary of the pull request.
Calls started from the World connect again: the call servers were turning the World away, so the camera and microphone never came on.

Add project on the desktop now lists the instances on ForkMesh by name to add in one click, checks an instance address and fills in its name and logo, and offers the phone's Minimal, Standard and Everything plugin packs.
Merging an agent's branch from the web or cleaning up a task's work now deletes that agent's scratch folder too, so finished agents no longer fill your disk.

Claude Code and Codex now give each new run a short title and branch name the way Claude's desktop app does, using a small fast model first; Cloudflare naming is off unless you turn it on in Settings > Agents.
Merging an agent no longer leaves a second agent with the same name in the Agents list.
When your microphone or camera is on, a live chart scrolls your frame rate, mic level, tracking time and round trip, and a blinking On air sign shows under your face in the corner and on your avatar.

Your camera now moves your uploaded avatar photo instead of the drawn face, both on your body and in the top-right corner, and arms and hands follow you more steadily, including how far forward you reach.
Reactions from gestures and the voice panel now pop on everyone's screen with a bouncing emoji burst, yours included.

The Genie spider now lives in the World: it follows you around and plays 100 different games with you, other people, Forkbot, the fountain, the campfire, bikes, cars, boards and more. Turn it off in World settings.

Desktop Settings now has a Halloween theme section under General that search finds, with the switch for everyone and its turn-off time for administrators and moderators, and the heading you jumped to lights up on the page like its entry in the list.

With several desktops running, the iPhone shows each one's status on the Desktops page, lets you pick which one runs your prompts in Where it runs, and stacks the desktops and core nodes in the icon above the clock.
The iPhone app stays signed in to your instances after the phone restarts.
Two tiny charts under the Dynamic Island show your agents' tokens in and out each second, and each agent's tile border now moves smoothly with its live token flow.
Send to agent on a failed run's log now sends the failing step and the end of the log, where the error is, instead of its first lines.
Logs → Desktop has a slider under the CPU and memory gauges that sets how much of the computer agents may use, and the new limit applies at once to agents already running.
A second desktop signed in to the same account can now sign owner actions after you switch accounts, and the Account switched message says whether they are on.
A phone you paired with a code before signing in can now manage your desktop's hosts once it signs in to the same account, instead of being told only the owner can.
The Usage page offers Install Claude Code or Install Codex when that tool is missing, and the debug bar has a live chart of UI stalls.
A desktop Actions step can now set timeout-minutes, and the desktop client CI build gets enough time to finish instead of stopping at 90 minutes.

Rebuild & restart is faster: it keeps its own compile cache that agent builds no longer push out, a new commit no longer recompiles two of the app's largest files, and the restart notice says how many compiles came from the cache.

The slow USB drive warning now says which port to move the drive to: it finds the computer's free faster ports, says when one is USB-C and where it sits, names what is using them when they are taken, and catches 10 Gbps drives like the SanDisk Extreme whose names give no hint.
Running a workflow from the Workflows page now jumps to Recent runs, selects the new run and shows its output on the right, updating live while it runs.

Video Mix DJ Studio now runs inside the desktop app as a full DJ studio with up to four YouTube decks, EQ, filters, echo, reverb and flanger, hot cues, beat loops, scratching, AUTOMIX, AUTO DJ, playlists and jam sessions.
When ForkMesh finds a disk labelled TMP that is not set to mount at startup, it asks for your password once and adds it to /etc/fstab, so the fast scratch disk is there after every reboot.
The Linux installer now installs Qt WebEngine, so YouTube, the Browser tab and agent browser windows play inside the app, and the next rebuild picks it up without clearing the build.
Emails from ForkMesh now come from founders@forkmesh.com, so replying to one reaches the team.
Signing up now sends your verification email once, instead of a new one each time the request was repeated.
The affiliate program's terms now say which tax form to send before a commission is paid: W-9 for US persons, W-8BEN for non-US individuals or W-8BEN-E for non-US companies.
The Tour plugin lets you choose Essentials, Advanced or The whole shebang, and on iPhone each stop is a live copy of the screen it describes that you can try before opening the real one.
In the desktop Market you can switch between a grid and a list, and clicking a package opens its details in a pane on the right.
Direct calls can use your avatar as your face, and group calls now apply your chosen face and voice on every connection.
Mirrored issues link back to the original on GitHub or Gitea, show the imported avatars, and can list threads newest first with their last commenters (the Forum-style issue lists plugin).
Long issue threads open faster: the page arrives with the whole thread, sent in parts, and the dashboard takes it over in place.

Instances can turn on Atom feeds of a repository's issues, a lite view of every thread that works without JavaScript, and a forum-style home page (the Feeds and lite view plugin); white label is an install setting.
Repositories can set a goal for independent mirrors, see how healthy each listed mirror is, and ask readers to run one (the Mirror goal plugin).
Images and files in mirrored GitHub threads are copied into the repository, so issue pages show them without loading anything from GitHub (the Mirrored attachments plugin).
Posts in other languages get a Translate bar that translates on your device or shows the instance's own English translation, and members can add their own translations (the Translations plugins).
Issue pages load faster on mirrored forums: imported avatars are cached, names are checked in one request per page, and Translate bars appear without slowing the thread.
Merging a pull request or updating its branch from the web shows each step live, from handing it to a mirror to publishing the result.
Links to a channel or direct message open it even on a freshly loaded chat page.
In a chat room the desktop prompt bar highlights its chat button, since that is what Enter sends with.
Agents on the Agents page can now open, read and type into terminal tabs in the desktop, without you approving the ForkMesh MCP server first.
Claude Code agents now show up as sessions in the Claude desktop app's Code tab, where you can read and resume them; use Open in Claude app from an agent's menu, or turn it off in Settings > Agents.
World retries with its lighter renderer when a computer's graphics cannot start the full 3D view, instead of going straight to the "could not start the 3D renderer" page.

Talk in the World with your microphone and camera: join the whole World, a World channel, a voice room you start, or a privacy bubble with the people next to you, while your camera moves your avatar's face, head and hands, hand gestures send reactions to whoever is speaking, and every speaker wears a live word count.
One channel list now holds the World channels, voice rooms, Office rooms, your channels and your direct messages, and opens conversations right in the World.
Turning on your camera in the World now works; the browser no longer blocks it.
A neighbour's hexagon with a bug terrarium now draws in about a third of the steps it used to, so the World runs smoother near it.

Administrators and moderators can switch on a Halloween theme in Settings, Appearance: green turns orange, a spider web and a witch-hatted Genie appear, and it switches itself off at the time they pick.
Instances can let people sign up without an email address, using a one-time recovery code, suggest random usernames, and appoint moderators who approve first posts, block accounts and lock threads.
Instances can use a GitHub-style theme that follows each visitor's light or dark system setting, and Settings, Appearance has a System choice.
A new install asks for nothing at launch: a short screen explains which permissions may come up and why, and each one is asked only when you first use the feature that needs it.
In the desktop's live database Visualizer, clicking a table opens that table in the Database tab.

In the new desktop design, Control, Network, Repos, Git, Files, Memory, Tasks, Chat, Settings, Users, Pings, Ledger, Analytics, Market, Stats, Health, Calendar, Specials and Calories are restyled to match, with a board view for tasks, a node detail panel, a places column in Files, repository cards, a Market grid, wallet QR codes in Ledger, a relay switcher in the sidebar and a table in Settings for choosing where each app shows up.

The debug bar's Report and Send diagnostic buttons are now one Diagnose button that turns red when it spots a performance, security or UI problem, and one click starts an agent with the model you have selected.
Merge all with AI now rebuilds a pull request from a stacked series whose earlier parts were already merged, instead of leaving it out because its code is not on this computer.
The install line on the homepage has a small Binary / Source switch, so you can copy the command that compiles ForkMesh from source.
Switching theme or interface from the View menu is several times faster and no longer freezes the window for many seconds.

The desktop prompt now names the chat channel you are in, with a menu to switch channel that shows each channel's users and chats, its three preview lines show the latest chat messages with channel, name and time, the send-to button reads chat, and the pop-out button is gone: drag the prompt by any part of its body to move it anywhere or out into its own window, and resize it from any edge or corner.

The desktop app freezes less while the disk is busy: Action logs and run status, saved-search runs and quick-fix choices are written in the background, and the Genie spider no longer rewrites your settings each time it wanders.
Drag a pinned workflow between the top, left, right and bottom strips, and drag a left-rail icon back onto the repository tab bar or Code toolbar.
The desktop's View menu can reset the look to the default a fresh install starts with, or match the theme of the instance you are connected to.

A spare disk labelled TMP now takes agent scratch folders, build caches and Action sandboxes, is cleaned on every start, can be erased from Settings, and shows in the debug bar alongside a warning when a USB drive is plugged into a slower port than it supports.
The Restart button now tells you which changed files it rebuilt, or that nothing changed since the last build.

The right-hand rail is now a side rail you fill yourself: drag workflows, special agents, pages and links onto it, open a small browser beside it, and open terminals as tabs in the window from it or the top bar, which Claude Code and your agents can read and type into while you share them.
The desktop app uses less CPU while agents or Actions run, and the Team page opens without reading every teammate's whole transcript.

On the desktop's Network page, the Nodes list now shows every saved host, fleet server, runner, relay and self-hosted instance (such as OWASP BLT), each on two lines with an icon per stat and CPU, RAM and disk first, and the Hosts controls sit in a compact rail beside it.
The composer's channel picker now lists your direct messages and has Message someone, so you can send a prompt straight to a person.
Tables with a very long value no longer freeze the window while they draw, and a busy workflow's output no longer stutters the app.
Notes open in the rendered preview; switch to Write to edit.
Success and error notices close themselves after 5 seconds, with a ring around the close button that fills as the time runs out; hover a notice to keep it open.
The version at the bottom right of the desktop app now also shows the short commit the build is on.

The terminal button in the top bar now opens a shell straight away in a pane on the right, with tabs, a + button for another shell and a menu for Claude Code or Codex, and Codex started there can read and type into your shared terminals like Claude Code.

The Workflows page shows special agents and your workflows in one list, with list, thumbnail and compact grid views, the latest output and run, pin, schedule and on/off controls under every workflow, and any workflow can now be pinned to a rail or run with an assignment.

Logs → Desktop now shows each CPU thread's load, clock and temperature, split into performance and efficiency cores, beside the CPU governor, energy preference, turbo, memory pressure, huge page and swap settings.
Long data tables no longer freeze for a second or two when a cell updates.
Clicking someone in the admin Users list opens a profile panel on the right with their picture and everything the directory knows about them, and every row now shows a picture.
On a large diff the scroll bar now shows where you are in the whole diff, so it no longer jumps up each time the next part loads, and dragging it moves through the entire diff.
The Git page's side-by-side diff has arrows between the two sides of each change: → reverts that change (or unstages it), ← stages it.
The Browser tab and side browser now show pages inside the app in a Chromium with Google's background services switched off, and typed searches go to DuckDuckGo.
Each ping on the desktop's Pings page shows the project's logo and a small icon saying whether it came from this desktop or your cloud inbox.
Instances can publish a static, read-only copy of their issues to GitHub Pages, Codeberg Pages or any host, and can turn on a Tor onion address.
Instances have a privacy mode: nothing about visitors is logged or sent, and the footer says so.
The Start your own instance page has a one-line prompt you can paste into Claude Code or another coding agent, which then sets up your instance with you.
Deploy nodes runs deploy again when Action sandboxes are on a TMP disk.
Feed posts have a Copy link button and a link to the post's public page on the website, which anyone can open without signing in.

On iPhone, Video Mix DJ Studio lets you hold a queued song for a menu that removes it, drags a queued song onto a deck as soon as you move your finger, and plays a song you add right away when nothing is playing.
iPhone video calls switch to the other person's picture as soon as it arrives, play through the loudspeaker, and the microphone test now plays back what you said.
Pull requests show a green, orange or red merge status button at the top, a compact icon-based Reviewers list, and no longer repeat the repository's Fork and Star bar.
Issues have an Assign button next to Comment, and contributors can take a second issue once they have a pull request open for the first.
The pull request review prompt now links a working diff and a plain-text page with every comment, and asks for feedback written to the author, or a short approval when nothing needs to change.

**Everyone enters the World.** Guests and members share the Town Square, see live avatar movement, and can use the embedded public World chat without leaving the scene.
**Resilient repository routes.** Public smart-HTTP traffic is proxied through healthy, signed mirrors with automatic failover and round-robin selection.
**SSH Git access.** Users can register an OpenSSH public key and clone or push through the permission-checked Git gateway; private keys remain on their own device.
**Non-custodial community rewards.** Contributors can fund the transparent public Solana pool directly from a self-custodial wallet. ForkMesh never stores contributor or node-operator private keys.
**Privacy-safe identity.** Clothing badges use optional approximate country, browser, and operating-system symbols without publishing raw IP addresses or precise location.
**Operational clarity.** World notifications, repository integrity proofs, security scan scope, and infrastructure metaphors link back to the technical state they represent.
**Built-in coding agents.** Assign any issue to Claude Code or Codex from the issue detail or quick-add box. The agent works on your connected fork and opens a pull request when it's done.
**A real terminal, in the app.** A native VT100 terminal renders every agent and workflow run with full color output and emoji.
**Legacy issue bounties.** This release originally added a custodial issue-bounty flow. That flow has since been retired: please do not send funds to historical bounty addresses.
**VS Code Marketplace plugin.** Optionally browse issues and kick off ForkMesh agents from your editor without installing the plugin in the base desktop app.
**Profile pages.** Click any node to see its full public profile — repos, identity, and version.
**Hardened by default.** Tighter signup and relay security, with auto-publish off until you say so.
**Parallel agents, no queue.** Run multiple agents at once across your issues.
**Continue the conversation.** Pick a session back up where it left off, with auto-PR creation on quick tasks.
**Live activity indicators.** See which agents are working right now.
**Issues and PRs that talk to each other.** Merge a PR and its linked issue closes itself; sync straight to main with one checkbox.
**One-click delegation.** Send any issue to your agent of choice — pre-filled and ready to go.
**Guest-first access.** Visitors enter the world immediately; registered accounts use email, password, and email verification.

**Solana payouts and contributions.** Publish a self-custodial payout address or voluntarily fund the public mainnet-beta community pool with a direct transfer signed in your own wallet. ForkMesh never receives a community member’s wallet key.
**Rewards for mirroring.** Eligible, integrity-verified nodes may be selected for a community incentive; participation, payment, and financial returns are never guaranteed.
**Network presence, done right.** Mirror-sync notices moved into a proper network log, with live connection alerts.
**Pull requests.** Signed patch submissions, browsable on the web and mergeable from the client.
**Actions.** Run shell-step workflows on push on your own desktop, with the latest live log one click away.
**Releases and tags.** See your tags, mark the current one, and cut new releases in seconds.
**Browse before you mirror.** Explore files, commits, and rich diffs (images side by side) — no clone required.
**ForkMesh on your phone.** Browse repositories, follow activity, chat, and submit signed collaboration updates. The mobile app is an access client; Git mirroring remains a desktop/headless-node job.
**Fork with intent.** Choose exactly where a fork lands in your working tree.
**A distributed mirror network.** Local Git mirrors, signed identities, and a Cloudflare relay that coordinates without ever holding your objects.
**A public catalog.** Public repositories and clearly labeled external stubs, with actively mirrored repository bytes streamed over HTTPS from a selected healthy origin.
**Issues that grow with you.** Open/closed states, priorities, custom fields, a Kanban board, and milestones with progress bars.
**Commit history and diffs**, viewable right in the browser.

**Authenticated shared-key room chat.** Genesis shipped client-encrypted transport whose default passphrase the relay could derive. Current public channels intentionally retain that integration-compatible boundary; private channels and direct messages now add automatic device-recipient encryption beyond it. Persisted frames remain limited to 500 per room for 7 days.
**One-click hand-off to your AI tools**, baked in from day one.
